subject: Performance SLO & Concurrency requirements - Acme integration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@acme.com>, Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & Concurrency requirements - Acme integration

Thanks for the call earlier today - great conversation. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and what we need from both sides for a pilot.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: embed Assistant in product for realtime recommendation flows (customer support routing + prod search reranking).
- Traffic profile (from Acme): steady baseline with predictable peak during business hours.
- Key asks: low 95th-pctl latency for streaming responses, support for long-lived streaming conversations (~30-60s), and ability to handle several hundred concurrent requests.

Acme targets we discussed (please confirm):
- 95th-pctl latency target: <= 300 ms for streaming token delivery (end-to-end for first tokens ideally < 200 ms).
- Average sustained throughput: ~200 QPS; short-term peaks up to 1,200 QPS.
- Concurrency requirement: 350-500 parallel requests (simultaneous in-flight requests across product).
- Connection pattern: client uses connection pooling (~30-60 persistent connections from each app server), multiple in-flight requests per connection.

What we need from Acme to size pilot and quota:
1) Confirm which model(s) you'll trial (token sizes / avg tokens per request / typical response length).
2) Confirm peak concurrency target you'd like provisioned for pilot (pick conservative number or desired target).
3) Any hard latency SLAs or we should treat these as SLO targets for evaluation.

Attached: SLO worksheet (slo-worksheet.xlsx) with fields filled from today's call - please fill the tokens/response-size columns and return.

Next steps
- Ethan/Sofia: confirm model + avg token sizes and pilot concurrency target.
- Laura (solutions eng): will propose preliminary quota/limits for pilot and a load-test plan.
- I'll provision the sandbox and put together an addendum for the pilot (DocuSign link once agreed).

Thanks - Marissa

--

From: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@acme.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency requirements - Acme integration

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 2:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Thanks for the call earlier today - great conversation. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and what we need from both sides for a pilot.
>
> ...

Thanks Marissa - this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- Model: we'll start with a fine-tuned open-llama 33B variant for production-like tests. Typical request payloads are ~120 tokens; responses average ~220 tokens but can go longer for some reranking tasks (up to ~600 tokens in rare cases).
- Traffic: baseline ~200 QPS as you noted. During promos/peaks we see bursts up to ~1,200 QPS but we can gate traffic to our desired max (we're aiming to keep steady peaks <= 600 QPS for the pilot).
- Concurrency: the app uses connection pooling (we maintain ~50 persistent HTTP/2 connections across our pool), and each connection can have multiple concurrent requests. Our engineering team measures "concurrency" as total in-flight requests across all app servers - we'd like Redwood to support 400 concurrent in-flight requests as the baseline pilot target, with the ability to burst to 700 for short periods (10-30 minutes).
- Streaming: streaming is required; many of our flows rely on partial token delivery. Typical streaming durations will be 10-60s depending on the request.

Can Redwood support: 400 guaranteed concurrency, 700 burstable for 30 minutes/day, and per-minute rate limits increased during the pilot? If so, we'd love to run a 2-week pilot with production traffic shape turned on.

Thanks - Ethan
Head of Integrations | Acme Corp
ethan.blake@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@acme.com>, Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency requirements - Acme integration

Marissa / Ethan - thanks for the extra detail. Copying Aditya (infra) to confirm feasibility and to propose concrete quota numbers.

Quick technical clarifications (Aditya - can you weigh in?):
- Token sizes: Ethan says avg request 120 tokens / avg response 220 tokens (peaks to 600). Are these within expected memory/KV-cache footprint for the 33B variant?
- Batch behavior: will Acme batch multiple logical requests into a single model call or send independent RPCs per user request? This affects peak GPU concurrency and kernel selection.
- Connection behavior: given ~50 persistent connections and multiple in-flight requests per connection, do you expect any NAT/load-balancer limit behavior on your side that would concentrate connections?

Preliminary Redwood pilot offer (subject to confirmation):
- Provisioned concurrency quota: 400 concurrent in-flight requests guaranteed (this maps to our request-queue concurrency setting).
- Burst capability: up to 750 concurrent in-flight requests for short bursts (up to 30 minutes per day) - we can tune burst windows based on observed traffic.
- Rate limits: baseline 10,000 requests/minute; allow temporary increase to 12,000 requests/minute during burst windows.
- Streaming support: full streaming with per-connection keepalive of 90s; chunked delivery supported for long-duration responses.
- Monitoring: we'll stand up a sandbox tenant with Grafana dashboards and token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

Next technical steps:
1) Aditya to confirm memory/KV cache implications for the 33B config and whether we need a smaller quantized variant for pilot.
2) Acme to fill in the SLO worksheet fields for token distributions and peak windows.
3) We'll schedule a 30-minute load-test plan review next week to validate our limits and confirm rollback thresholds.

Aditya - any constraints on the burst duration or the per-minute RPM that would change the numbers above?

Thanks - Laura

--
Laura Bennett

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency requirements - Acme integration

Thanks all - putting the agreed items into one place so we can move to the DocuSign addendum and pilot provisioning.

Agreed pilot configuration (summary)
- Provisioned concurrency: 400 concurrent in-flight requests (guaranteed).
- Burst concurrency: up to 750 concurrent in-flight requests for up to 30 minutes/day (we can reconfigure windows after initial tests).
- Rate limits: baseline 10,000 req/min; burst allowed up to 12,000 req/min.
- Streaming: supported with 90s keepalive and chunked token delivery.
- Monitoring & SLOs: sandbox Grafana + token-level latency dashboards; we will measure 95th-pctl streaming latency (initial target <= 300 ms; goal to optimize towards 200 ms).

Action items & timeline
- Acme (Ethan/Sofia): confirm token distribution columns in slo-worksheet.xlsx and sign the pilot addendum (DocuSign link). Target: return by Thurs 6/18.
- Redwood (Laura/Aditya): validate memory/kv footprint for 33B variant and finalize load-test plan. Target: technical review by Tue 6/16.
- Marissa: will provision sandbox and send DocuSign once we confirm numbers. Pilot target start date: 2026-06-22.

Attachments: acme-mop-draft.pdf (pilot addendum draft), slo-worksheet.xlsx (updated from call).

If everyone confirms, I'll kick off provisioning this week.

Best - Marissa
